title: Judging the artist versus the man: Beethoven's Nephew
summary: Freeman resists discussing Goodman's personality, citing Beethoven, and prefers to credit the good he did; Dance argues biography needs the person.

story.theme_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the leader and his bands
story.community_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the perfectionist bandleader

blocks.x: No, well, of course, there are many things -- you see, I don't want to get into the personal things here. I don't like -- I haven't liked too much talking about Benny Goodman as a person, because I don't think really that it's any of my business.

Well, the only thing is this, Bud, this is history in a way, and you know, when you see a biography on anybody, if you were to try to divorce their life from them - themselves, you are getting half a picture.
As you said Lester is telling his own story when he blows --
Yes, but I think if Lester had been an unkind man, I wouldn't have said anything. I would have just told you about his playing, but there was an element there

Now, if you want something again analogous to this idea, there is a marvelous book written by two psychiatrists, a man and wife, and I cannot think of their names, but the book was called Beethoven's Nephew. Now, just go and listen to music. Get the nine symphonies and listen to them all -- I have them all -- and you just wonder where this heavenly music could have come from, because Beethoven was a monster as a person.
And it's about well, he drives his young nephew almost to an asylum and the monstrous things he did, but look at the music.

So is the man his music, I doubt it very much, or is the music the man, you see. So what right have we really, I think it's best that we think of Benny Goodman as a great artist, having given a lot of great music to the world and forget what he was like as a man, with all due respect to what you are looking for in the interview, Helen.

All I was thinking is a positive aspect, what I was -- now, when we said about Benny, we all know that there have been some odd things said about Benny so when we say that we think it was the size of his talent and so on, that made it difficult for him to relate to the way ordinary people were, to me that's a positive statement to make. But
Well, let me say one simple thing here. Let us try to find out about the wonderful things he did for people.
